raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# Description

We need fail cases where we expect CuTeDSL kernels are used to avoid silent fallbacks like #3743 catches. This also introduces a breaking change that `NVTE_WARN_IF_CUTEDSL_BACKEND_NOT_CHOSEN` is changed to `NVTE_REPORT_IF_CUTEDSL_BACKEND_NOT_CHOSEN` which can warn or fail the test.

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Changes

Please list the changes introduced in this PR:

- Report CuTeDSL kernels falling back with a warn or fail option based on the env var
- 2D quantization is currently unsupported so for this it won't trigger warn or fail and I added a TODO to remind me of adding this kernel later
- Add cuda-bindings in setup.py since it's used by quantize_mxfp8.py and fused_mla_q_uproj
- Make CI scripts fail if falling back to CUDA

# Checklist:

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [x] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

nodes.body:
Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Medium impact]** The PR appears safe to merge; no new actionable defects were found.

Summary

Adds `NVTE_REPORT_IF_CUTEDSL_BACKEND_NOT_CHOSEN` to choose between warnings and errors when enabled CuTeDSL requests fall back. - CuTeDSL fallback can warn or fail when the backend is enabled. - L0 tests fail when enabled CuTeDSL requests fall back. Reviews (5) · Last reviewed commit: ["Merge branch 'main' into warn\_or\_fail\_wh..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/6a16b8b7f2bb0a3b6f1fa4367b4acbb6f98979d4) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

**Backend comparison tests fail** With CuTeDSL built and enabled, this global setting breaks the existing CUDA-versus-CuTeDSL tests. `tests/pytorch/mxfp8/test_mxfp8_cutedsl_backend.py` calls `set_cutedsl_backend(False)` to compute its CUDA reference. That call now throws “the CuTeDSL backend is disabled” before the comparison can run. The JAX tests do the same and inherit the same setting from `qa/L0_jax_unittest/test.sh`. Allow intentional CUDA reference calls while keeping strict checks for the CuTeDSL calls. The reporting level is read once, so changing the environment after the first native call will not fix this. **Knowledge Base Used:** [CuTeDSL kernel backend](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/native-cutedsl.md)

My earlier comment was based on the previous behavior; it doesn’t apply here.

nodes.body: It's used by `quantize_mxfp8.py` and `fused_mla_q_uproj.py`. `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` should always depends on this but I think it's clearer to explicitly mark this as a dependency

In that case we should also mark `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` and `tvi-ffi` as required dependencies. Currently those are user installed, which is fine because this is an optional backend. So for consistency either all or none should be included.

files.patch:
@@ -153,11 +153,13 @@ General
                  It also requires ``apache-tvm-ffi``, ``nvidia-cutlass-dsl`` to be installed and you are using CPython 3.10 or later.
                  If these requirements are not met, Transformer Engine will fall back to using CUDA C++ kernels if possible.
 
-.. envvar:: NVTE_WARN_IF_CUTEDSL_BACKEND_NOT_CHOSEN
+.. envvar:: NVTE_REPORT_IF_CUTEDSL_BACKEND_NOT_CHOSEN
 
-   :Type: ``int`` (0 or 1)
-   :Default: ``0``
-   :Description: Warn when TE falls back to the CUDA C++ kernels instead of dispatching to available CuTeDSL kernels. Useful to verify if the CuTeDSL path is taken.
+   :Type: ``str`` (``WARN`` or ``ERROR``)
+   :Default: None
+   :Description: Control what happens when TE fails dispatch to a CuTeDSL kernel and would fall back to the CUDA C++ kernel.
+                 ``WARN`` emits a warning explaining why CuTeDSL kernels are unavailable and falls back to CUDA kernels. ``ERROR`` raises an error and fails instead.
+                 Only effective when the CuTeDSL backend is enabled (see :envvar:`NVTE_ENABLE_CUTEDSL_BACKEND`).
 
 .. envvar:: NVTE_GROUPED_TENSOR_HANDLE_POOL_SIZE_MB

@@ -12,6 +12,9 @@ mkdir -p "$XML_LOG_DIR"
 TE_LIB_PATH=$(pip3 show transformer-engine | grep -E "Location:|Editable project location:" | tail -n 1 | awk '{print $NF}')
 export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$TE_LIB_PATH:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
 
+# If CuTeDSL backend is not enabled, this will be ignored
+export NVTE_REPORT_IF_CUTEDSL_BACKEND_NOT_CHOSEN=ERROR
+
 # Set parallelization parameters
 NUM_PHYSICAL_CORES=$(nproc)
 NUM_PARALLEL_JOBS=4

@@ -21,6 +21,9 @@ FAILED_CASES=""
 
 export NVTE_JAX_TEST_TIMING=1
 
+# If CuTeDSL backend is not enabled, this will be ignored
+export NVTE_REPORT_IF_CUTEDSL_BACKEND_NOT_CHOSEN=ERROR
+
 pip3 install "nltk>=3.8.2,!=3.10.1" || error_exit "Failed to install nltk"
 pip3 install pytest==8.2.1 pytest-timeout==2.4.0 || error_exit "Failed to install pytest dependencies"

@@ -27,6 +27,9 @@ export NVTE_FLASH_ATTN_V2=1
 export NVTE_FLASH_ATTN_V3=0
 export NVTE_FLASH_ATTN_V4=0
 
+# If CuTeDSL backend is not enabled, this will be ignored
+export NVTE_REPORT_IF_CUTEDSL_BACKEND_NOT_CHOSEN=ERROR
+
 pip3 install pytest==8.2.1 || error_exit "Failed to install pytest"
 
 python3 -m pytest --tb=auto --junitxml=$XML_LOG_DIR/pytest_test_optional_flash_attn_import.xml $TE_PATH/tests/pytorch/test_optional_flash_attn_import.py || test_fail "test_optional_flash_attn_import.py"
